title: Edge Sampling Inspector: tail-aware sampling proxy to reduce tracing hotpath overhead
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: As traffic grows, the cost and latency impact of full hotpath tracing has increased. Current onboard/offboard samplers either run on the service hotpath (increasing p99 latency and allocations) or as deferred background workers that lack visibility into connection-level signals and tail anomalies. We need a lightweight, topology-aware component that makes early low-cost sampling decisions using edge signals and can promote suspect requests for rich trace capture without adding measurable latency to normal requests.

Goal: Build "Edge Sampling Inspector" — a small proxy/sidecar that sits at the ingress (LB or service mesh sidecar) and performs inexpensive, heuristic + ML-informed prefiltering. It will: (1) run sub-microsecond prefix checks and score requests for tail-likelihood, (2) tag or uplift selected requests for full tracing downstream, (3) emit compact sampling events to our metrics/log pipeline for telemetry and online tuning, and (4) provide operators dashboards showing sampled tail patterns and sampling budget utilization.

Success metrics: reduce tracing-related hotpath CPU allocations by >=40% on high-QPS services, keep added p99 request latency < 0.1ms 95% of the time, and improve tail-trace capture rate (+50% of SLO-violating requests have full traces captured) while keeping total trace volume within budgeted quotas.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable proxy binary (Go) with <100KB steady-state memory per instance and no allocations on common fast-path checks
Proxy can classify requests using a lightweight feature set (route, headers, basic payload fingerprints) and decide: sample-now, sample-defer, or bypass
Integration with tracing headers (W3C tracestate & traceparent) to tag requests for downstream full-context capture
Compact sampling telemetry emitted to metrics pipeline (Prometheus counters + JSON event to logs pipeline) for per-service sampling rate and tail-score histograms
Alerting rule + Grafana panel that surfaces when sampling budgets are exhausted or tail-capture ratio degrades
Automated A/B rollout: can be enabled via feature flag per cluster and rolled back with no service restarts
Benchmarks demonstrating <0.1ms p99 added latency and >=40% reduction in tracer allocations for instrumented services
implementation_notes: Prototype as an Envoy filter for Istio/Consul mesh and a separate tiny Go sidecar for non-mesh environments.
Keep hotpath code in straight-line, allocation-free paths: avoid maps/allocating strings; use fixed byte slices and precompiled regex/filters where necessary.

Tail score model v1: simple logistic regression with features: route, header-token-presence, payload-length-bucket, previous-retry-count. Host this model as compiled weights embedded in the binary; no network call in the hotpath.
Telemetry sink: Prometheus counters labelled by service/route/sampling_decision, and an aggregated JSON event to our logs pipeline to feed the Optimize tuning job.
Fallback: when sampling budget exhausted or model disabled, proxy should fall back to configured deterministic sampling (e.g., 0.01%).
Security: ensure tracestate pieces added by us are HMAC-signed per team convention to prevent spoofing (configurable by deployment to opt-out in private/on-prem clusters).
Compatibility: preserve existing tracing header semantics and support multiple tracing vendors downstream (Zipkin/OTLP/Datadog).
Build plan: library + tests, integration harness against local jaeger/collector, benchmark harness that simulates 10k RPS for p99 latency and allocation profiles.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Built prototype Envoy filter that computes route+header features in <200ns per request at 100k RPS simulation. Memory profile looks good (bootstrap binary 1.6MB). - Aisha

2026-02-18: Decided to embed logistic regression weights in binary for v1 to avoid hotpath RPCs. Security team requested HMAC scheme for tracestate additions; engineering to add opt-out config. - Liam

2026-02-26: Benchmarks vs instrumented service: tracer allocations reduced by ~45% when proxy marks 70% of requests as bypass; p99 added latency measured at 0.07ms on c5-large instance. Running longer soak tests. - Morgan

2026-03-05: Integration with metrics pipeline complete; initial Grafana dashboard created showing per-service sampling rates and tail-score distribution. Need product/observability feedback on alert thresholds. - Liam
2026-03-11: Canary rollout to staging cluster started (10% of ingress). Observed 3 SLO-failure traces uplifted for fuller capture; sampling budget telemetry accurate. No regressions so far. - Evan
blockers: Finalizing HMAC header format with security (waiting on security review sign-off)
Edge cases for WebSocket upgrade flows where header propagation differs — need network infra guidance
Performance regression guardrails in some low-memory appliances (on-prem boxes) require memory cap config
notes_for_review: Please review the HMAC tracestate approach and the embedded-model update path. Ops should validate the budget tuning dashboard before production rollout. Perf team: confirm allocation numbers on arm64 builders too.
